proposal: The Mandate recommends RCRA changes: create a post-closure care permit tailored to post-closure obligations, modify regulations that impede recycling and reuse by providing an alternative pathway to hazardous waste regulation for transport to legitimate recyclers, move the e-Manifest system to 100 percent electronic and eliminate paper manifests, reassign RCRA air emission standards to the air office, and restructure the Office of Land and Emergency Management, including eliminating the Office of Emergency Management and moving the emergency management function into the homeland security function under the Administrator's office, moving removal authority into the Superfund remediation office and dropping Emergency Management from the office name (pp. 432-433).
remaining: A final Paper Manifest Sunset Rule and the end of paper manifests (p. 432)
An RCRA post-closure care permit tailored to post-closure obligations (p. 432; none found)
A general alternative pathway for transport of materials to legitimate recyclers (p. 432; none found)
Reassignment of RCRA section 3004 air emission standards to the air office (p. 432; none found)
Elimination of the Office of Emergency Management and reassignment of its functions (p. 433; a merger with Superfund was reported, which differs)

review.mandate_note: Pages 432 to 433 ask for a tailored RCRA post-closure permit, a rule giving recyclable materials an alternative pathway outside hazardous waste regulation, an all-electronic manifest system, reassignment of RCRA section 3004 air standards to the air office, and OLEM restructuring that eliminates the Office of Emergency Management, moves emergency management under the Administrator's homeland security function and removal authority to the Superfund office, and drops Emergency Management from the name. The draft said functions would move toward Homeland Security, which reads as the separate department, so the wording was corrected; this is a clarification, not a change in substance.

status_summary: On 2026-03-05 EPA proposed a Paper Manifest Sunset Rule that would stop accepting paper hazardous waste manifests 24 months after a final rule, with comments due 2026-05-04; no final rule had appeared by 2026-10-15. On 2026-03-23 EPA proposed a categorical non-waste determination under its non-hazardous secondary materials rules for recovered abandoned scrap tires burned as fuel in cement kilns, a narrow change related to the recycling recommendation. EPA announced updates to the Office of Land and Emergency Management on 2025-07-17 without structural details, and no post-closure permit rule, hazardous waste recycling pathway, air standards reassignment or elimination of the emergency management office was found.

timeline.event: EPA announced a next phase of organizational improvements that included updates to the Office of Land and Emergency Management; the release gave no structural details.
EPA proposed the Paper Manifest Sunset Rule, ending acceptance of paper hazardous waste manifests 24 months after a final rule (91 FR 10862).

EPA proposed a categorical non-waste determination under 40 CFR part 241 for recovered abandoned scrap tires burned in cement kilns and a revised definition of established tire collection program (91 FR 13804; comments due 2026-05-22).
